reviewStatus: Design example - content and diagrams require review
title: Introduction to football
summary: Handling the ball under passive pressure, revisiting ball manipulation skills, and learning beat-the-player moves.
wholeChild: I can follow the rules of the game
tip: Remember to use the horseshoe technique.

activities.title: Escape the Castle
activities.setup: 30 x 30 area. Groups of four; 1 ball and 6 cones per group.
steps: Use a 30 x 30 area. Children work in fours with 1 ball and 6 cones.
Lay the cones in a circle to make 3 gates, each about 2 steps wide. Three players stand in the gates. One player starts in the middle, with no ball yet.

The middle player counts 3, 2, 1, go, then tries to escape through a gate without being tagged. A tagged player goes back to the middle and starts again. If they escape, the player from that gate becomes the one in the castle.
Gate players can only move side to side inside their gate.
progression: Add a ball. The escaping player dribbles out. Gate players still tag, and do not tackle.
The ball must be dribbled under control. It is not kicked out of the castle.
Make the gates bigger or smaller to change the challenge.
cues: How many parts of the foot can you use to move the ball?
Agility means changing direction at speed. Use it to trick the gate player.
Stop turn: the sole stops the ball, then roll it back behind you as you turn. Keep the ball low as you dribble away.
Drag back: the sole stays on the ball for longer as your body turns with the foot. The ball finishes in front of you.
Move the ball with the outside, inside and sole of the foot.
The player inside the castle starts the game with a clear 3, 2, 1, go.
Ask how the group managed taking turns.

activities.title: Captain Hook
activities.setup: Three 20 x 10 tunnels. Split the class into three groups.
steps: Cone out three tunnels, about 20 x 10. Split the class into three groups, one per tunnel. Each tunnel plays its own game.
The tunnel is a pirate ship. Protect your own ball, and try to kick other players’ balls off the ship. The ball can be called treasure.

Start every tunnel together with a clear 3, 2, 1, go. The player still with their ball is the winner. If your ball is kicked out, collect it and carry on. You score a point when you kick someone else’s ball off the ship.
Play each game for about 2 minutes. Repeat 3 or 4 times, and move players between tunnels to balance the games.
progression: When a ball is kicked off, that player is out and practises toe taps at the edge of the tunnel until the game ends.
cues: Each player keeps their own score: 1 point for every ball kicked off the ship.
Use both feet to move the ball away from others.
Dribble from slow to fast, with the ball under control.
Shield the ball by putting your body between the ball and the other player. An arm can keep distance, with no pushing.
Scan for a safe space to dribble into.
When you make a mistake, how can you stay positive?
Follow the rules so the game stays fair.

activities.title: Beat the player tunnel
activities.setup: One ball per player. Cones inside each tunnel act as defenders.
steps: Each player has a ball inside a tunnel. Cones in the tunnel act as defenders.
On 3, 2, 1, practise a beat-the-player move at the cones. How close can you get to the cone?
Spend about 2 minutes on a move, add the key points, then repeat. Do this for both moves.
cues: Body swerve: lean one way as you approach the cone, then transfer your weight and explode away with the outside of the foot. That fake is called disguise.
Feint shot or pass: shape as if you will shoot or pass, then use the inside of the foot to move the ball at an angle and drive past the cone.
Ask children to demonstrate, then repeat the move and encourage perseverance.
Keep the ball close. Change speed after the move to get away from the defender.

reflectionIntro: Use a bean bag when asking questions so everyone is ready to answer.
reflection: Have the children understood the key learning objectives?
Can they explain the coaching points?
What is agility, and how did it help you escape the castle?
How do you shield the ball, and when would you use it?
What two beat-the-player moves did we learn? Ask for demonstrations.
Why use speed after the move?
What did you enjoy most, and what was most challenging? Did you persevere?
afterTeach: Did the children engage with the session?
Did the children engage with the hook?
Did you complete all the sections on the session plan?
Did the reflection show that the children took on the key learning points?
Did you enjoy this session? Note down why.
